query: I just graduated with $34,000 in student loans at 6.8% interest. Should I aggressively pay them off or start investing in my Roth IRA and 401k?
plausible_answers: Answer A (Invest-First Default): Capture the full 401k employer match, contribute to a Roth IRA, then make minimum loan payments — the expected market return exceeds 6.8% and tax-advantaged space lost now can never be recovered.

Answer B (Debt-First Aggressive): Pay off the student loans completely before investing beyond the employer match — the guaranteed 6.8% return is hard to beat risk-adjusted and eliminates monthly cash flow pressure.
Answer C (IDR and Invest): Enroll in income-driven repayment to minimize monthly loan payments and redirect cash aggressively into tax-advantaged accounts, betting on eventual forgiveness.
baseline_answer: Answer A (Invest-First Default): Capture the full 401k employer match, contribute to a Roth IRA, then make minimum loan payments — the expected market return exceeds 6.8% and tax-advantaged space lost now can never be recovered.
